text:
Sam: quick heads-up — i'm proposing a small change to the rerank API score semantics, want quick feedback before i draft a PR
Priya: what kind of change? normalized scores or extra metadata?
Sam: two parts: (1) switch primary score field to `score` in 0..1 normalized floats (legacy `raw_score` optional) and (2) add optional `score_units` for quota/telemetry (e.g. "candidate_unit")
Ethan: careful — our billing & quota plumbing currently assumes a single per-request cost. if we move to `score_units` we need to decide if units are per-candidate or aggregated per-request
Priya: agree. i'd prefer per-candidate units because cost correlates with candidate count and model fanout. console and alerts can then show per-candidate cost heatmaps
Lina: UI/UX note: if we add `score_units` we should expose a per-route toggle in the console: "Show candidate accounting" so small teams don't get overwhelmed by details
Ethan: routing implications: if scores are normalized, some routing heuristics that compare absolute raw scores will break. we need a mapping or enough meta to know model variant + scale
Sam: plan: add `score` (0-1), keep `raw_score` for backward compatibility, and attach `model_scale` field in response header (e.g. "small", "medium", "large") so router can apply correct thresholds
Priya: +1 on compatibility. telemetry asks: do we bucket scores on the client or server? we should do server-side buckets for consistent dashboards
Sam: server-side buckets. propose these metrics: `rerank.candidates.count`, `rerank.score.bucket_<0.1`, `rerank.score.bucket_0.1_0.3`, `rerank.score.bucket_0.3_0.6`, `rerank.score.bucket_0.6_1.0`, and `rerank.candidate_units`
Ethan: what about small vs large model routing? cost routing currently uses a per-request cost estimate. if we switch to per-candidate units we can route like: if candidates * unit_per_candidate > threshold -> route to cheaper quantized model or limit fanout
Lina: console rollout UX: add a canary slider for rerank routes (0-100%) + an override to force model_variant per-request. Also show estimated cost delta in the rollout dialog
Priya: need to update quota docs and console to show both "request quota" and "candidate quota". users asked for visibility when their topk grows unexpectedly
Sam: question for ops: does canary toggles already support percent-based traffic split for a single API route?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout feature enabled on routing service at 2026-03-19T14:12:03Z (ops-team). Use `route.canary_pct` flag in rollout config.
Ethan: sweet. then server can enforce a hard max candidates param per-tier and emit a `quota_violation` event when exceeded
Priya: sample request/response proposal (small):
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query_id": "q-123",
  "candidates": ["c1","c2",...],
  "top_k": 10,
  "model_variant": "auto"
}
```
```
200 OK
{
  "query_id": "q-123",
  "results": [
    {"id":"c2","score":0.93,"raw_score":3.1,"score_units":"candidate_unit","model_scale":"medium"},
    {"id":"c5","score":0.72,"raw_score":2.4,"score_units":"candidate_unit","model_scale":"medium"}
  ],
  "meta": {"candidate_units_total": 10}
}
```
Lina: for console telemetry: show sample score histogram, per-route candidate_units heatmap, and a routing-preview that shows which model variant would be chosen for example payloads
Sam: ops + infra: we also need a migration plan for clients. i suggest a 2-release approach: add fields and make `score` the preferred in docs, then after 3 months mark `raw_score` deprecated but still accepted
Ethan: agree. also update our integration tests + e2e to validate routing decisions based on `model_scale` header and `candidate_units_total`
Priya: one more edge: legacy consumers may rely on signed scores (higher negative better). we must ensure normalization preserves ordering. add a `score_normalization` enum in meta: {"linear", "softmax_logit"} so clients can interpret
Sam: good catch. will add that to the PR. anything else?
Lina: can we add a lightweight telemetry flag `rerank.sampled.debug=true` to emit one verbatim request/response per 1000 requests for debug without saving PII?
ops-bot: policy-bot: debug sampling must scrub PII fields. set default to 1/1000 sampling and require opt-in via enterprise config.
Ethan: ok then i'm happy. i'll sketch the router changes (threshold mapping for model_scale) and a fallback to `model_variant=cheap-quant` when budget exceeded
Sam: thanks all — i'll open the PR with the proposed schema, migration schedule, and console mockups. tag me for review :) :thumbsup:
